decision: REJECT (wrong lever; see run_05 discriminator-regularization fix)
summary: Hypothesis REJECTED: paw lift went to 2-4mm, if anything slightly worse than run_03's 3-9mm. Correct diagnosis found instead: discriminator score separation (expert +7.6 vs policy -7.6 to -8.2, i.e. ~15) has been near-saturated since early training in every run so far (run_01 through run_04 all show the same -7 to -8 policy score) -- classic AMP discriminator-dominance pathology, where a too-confident discriminator gives near-zero style-reward GRADIENT regardless of style_reward_scale (scaling ~0 by 2.5x is still ~0). This is why weight tuning didn't move anything.

REJECTED: discriminator loss floor unchanged (~0.03, same as every prior run) even at 3x the gradient penalty -- confirms this isn't primarily a discriminator-regularization-strength issue. Paw lift still 3.6-6.9mm, no real improvement. New hypothesis found instead: skrl_amp_cfg.yaml has fixed_log_std=True, initial_log_std=-2.9 (action std ~0.055 in normalized units, ~0.008 rad actual joint noise per step) carried over UNCHANGED from the prior rev_3-era tuning without reconsidering it for a freshly-initialized policy in a new env. With entropy_loss_scale=0.0 too, the policy has essentially no mechanism to ever explore into a large-amplitude stepping strategy -- it can only get there via gradient drift from a near-zero-swing initialization, which the (already-established) weak/saturated style gradient can't provide. This is a genuinely different, stronger hypothesis than run_03/04 (an exploration-starvation problem, not a reward-balance problem).
